Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

young adjective

of people

also young man, young woman, young people, when I was young, younger

classical

Quint. 4.2.42: est mihi fīlius juvenis (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 21.46.8

juvenis, juvenis

adjective and noun, third declension; comparative junior

young; a young man or woman

A grown young person, by the Roman count between about twenty and forty (Lewis & Short); “younger” is minor nātū (see younger).

Other words

  • adulēscēns, adulēscentis — young; a youth, a young man or woman

    adjective and noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 67: quamvīs sit adulēscēns; Traupman 410 · Declension on Wiktionary

    One still growing up, younger than a juvenis in the strict count, though the two overlap.

  • parvus, parva, parvum — little, young (of children)

    also used · classical · Traupman 410 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Of small children: cum parvus essēs, “when you were little” (see small).

Examples

  • hic erit juvenis penes quem perfectī hujusce bellī laus est

    this will be the young man who has the glory of finishing this warLiv. 21.46.8

  • parvus (parvulus) nātū

    young (in age)Traupman 410

  • jūnior, minor nātū

    youngerTraupman 410

  • juvenis

    a young man (roughly twenty to forty)Traupman 410

See also younger, youngest, small, old, adult.
